data.narrative:
OpenStar is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Ratu Mataira and Thomas Berry that has raised $35M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 nuclear energy firms (3 public, 8 private), including peers such as Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $35M as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $88M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied; while six same-sector comparables exist, fewer than three met narrow filters on stage, proximity, or valuation tier, making sector-wide median comparison uninformative.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $74M to $101M, with a median point of $88M. This range reflects standard seed-stage progression mechanics applied to disclosed fundraising. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient narrow-peer datapoints to cross-check the stage-progression result and the inherent volatility of pre-revenue nuclear technology valuations, where technical milestones and regulatory pathway clarity materially drive investor repricing.
